q: Your working life runs on Gmail, Drive and Docs. Which tool fits your daily workflow best?
explanation: Gemini is Google's assistant and is best when your working life runs on Gmail, Drive and Docs, because it sits naturally inside that ecosystem.

q: Mid-afternoon you hit ChatGPT's free message cap. What should you do?
options: Wait a while, or switch to another tool — switching costs nothing
Sign up for a paid plan immediately
Give up on AI for the rest of the week
Borrow a colleague's account to keep going
explanation: Free tiers cap messages and searches so the free ride stays free. When you hit a cap, wait — or switch tools, since switching costs nothing and you have four others.

q: Over the next few days of practice, which approach builds fluency fastest?
options: Hopping between all five tools in every session
Doing your practice in one primary tool and keeping the others on standby
Using whichever tool released the newest update
Reading reviews to find the 'best' tool before you start
explanation: Fluency beats tool-hopping: you judge a tool from use, not reviews. Practise in one primary tool — ChatGPT is the sensible default — and keep the rest on standby until the Day 5 head-to-head.
